text.p: Telco Communications Group Inc chief executive Donald Burns said Wednesday that "We are comfortable with the overall consensus estimates," regarding the company's prospects for the rest of 1997. First Call estimates for the company are $0.97 a share for 1997.
The First Call consensus estimate for the first quarter, which ended March 31, was $0.18 per share, which Telco bettered by $0.02 in results released today.
Burns also said that he believed that the long-distance carrier would achieve a revenue mix this year that will include more from its commercial sales division and less from its consumer division.
Sales from the commercial divisison, started in June, 1996, were $17 million in the quarter, versus $9.3 million in the quarter ended December 31.

Burns added that both revenue and operating expenses in the commercial sales division were ahead of plan, and that the division is well on its way to achieving break even profitability by the end of the year. He said the division is expected to contribute significantly to the company's future growth.

The company is also now focusing on its marketing efforts to maximize its revenue opportunities from both new and existing customers, he said. Telco's near-total reliance on saturation mailings has evolved to include targeted mailings to specific customer groups, expanded media advertising and customer membership programs, said Burns.
"While we still expect continued growth from our marketing activities, increased competition will reduce the consumer division's growth rate," he said.
That division reported sales of $105.4 million in the quarter, versus $88.9 million in the year-earlier period.
